answer:
Verdict: yes

The trace is consistent with a thundering herd on the shared futex: all 16 sink workers appear as waiters on the same futex address (`94518829081440`):

`sink-0` (645030), `sink-1` (645031), `sink-2` (645032), `sink-3` (645033), `sink-4` (645034), `sink-5` (645035), `sink-6` (645036), `sink-7` (645037), `sink-8` (645038), `sink-9` (645039), `sink-10` (645040), `sink-11` (645041), `sink-12` (645042), `sink-13` (645043), `sink-14` (645044), and `sink-15` (645045).

Their sampled states are dominated by waiting: each has about 19 seconds in “Wait blocked,” and roughly 8.4–9.1 seconds in “Wait for CPU.” The futex analysis also records 982,772 `WAKE` operations. That supports the herd interpretation, though the sampled results do not directly tie each application item to a particular wake-and-reblock sequence.
